nearbyCountiesFullText.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...Portions of Illinois, including the following counties in
Illinois, Cook, De Kalb, DuPage, Will, Grundy, Kane, Kendall, La
Salle, Lake, and Lee, as well as Lake County in Indiana.

* WHEN...Through this evening.

* IMPACTS...Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Flooding
of low lying and flood prone area.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Rain, heavy at times, is expected this afternoon into early this
evening. Rainfall totals of 2 inches or more in just a few hours
could occur within the more intense rainfall corridors. This
heavy rain, falling on already saturated soils, would likely
result in flooding, particularly in low lying and flood prone
areas.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
nearbyCountiesFullText.instruction:
A Flood Watch means flooding is possible, but not yet certain, based
upon the latest forecasts. Persons with interests along area rivers,
creeks, and other waterways should monitor the latest forecasts and
be prepared to take action should flooding develop.

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Northern Indiana
620 AM EDT Thu Oct 1 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Window of mostly dry weather outside of a few scattered
  showers will come to an end by this afternoon. Chances for
  showers (50-90%) and an isolated thunderstorms return this
  afternoon into the overnight period. Locally heavy rain is
  possible, but overall flood concerns continue to appear low 
  at this time. 

- Dry conditions are expected this weekend into early next week,
  with highs in the 60s, low 70s (warmest further south).
  Overnight lows will drop into the 40s. Tuesday morning looks
  to be the coldest night with lows dropping into the upper 30s.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 415 AM EDT Thu Oct 1 2026

Synoptic pattern continues to shift with the ridging to the
southeast pushing eastward over the next day or so. Troughing
over the northern CONUS will push southeast into the Great 
Lakes region and push the band of recent rain that has been in 
place just to our north and west south through the CWA beginning
today through tomorrow morning in the form of a cold front. A 
few embedded thunderstorms are possible with this frontal 
passage but lack of any decent shear and instability any storms
should remain weak but in any storms heavy downpours will be
possible especially with PWAT values around 1.75 to 2 inches.
WPC ERO has our area mainly under a marginal risk for excessive
rainfall but a small area mostly for the western portions of the
CWA is under a slight risk for excessive rainfall. 

In the wake of the front on Friday morning into the early 
afternoon cooler temperatures and drier conditions will arrive
and with a more zonal flow in place aloft shall continue through
the weekend into next week. Highs each day mainly in the 60s
with a few locations far south getting close to the 70 degree
mark. Lows will also drop into the 40s each night beginning 
Saturday morning. The coldest morning looks to be Tuesday with 
lows getting into the upper 30s. Time to make sure your furnaces
are tuned up for the season.

&&

.AVIATION /12Z TAFS THROUGH 12Z FRIDAY/...
Issued at 618 AM EDT Thu Oct 1 2026

VFR conditions expected to continue through the first half of
the period or so with scattered light rain showers moving
through just south of the main boundary that will begin to push
southward later today bringing a more consolidated band of
rain showers through the remainder of the TAF period and
lowering cigs to MVFR to IFR cats after 21z for KSBN and after
03z Fri with the cool frontal boundary pushing southward through
the CWA. 

&&

.IWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
IN...None.
OH...None.
MI...None.
MARINE...None.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION...Andersen

spc.summary: Locally strong/gusty winds and perhaps a brief tornado or two may occur this afternoon/early evening across parts of southern Kansas into northwest Oklahoma and vicinity.
spc.text:
SPC AC 011628

   Day 1 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1128 AM CDT Thu Oct 01 2026

   Valid 011630Z - 021200Z

   ...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS PARTS OF
   SOUTHERN KANSAS/NORTHERN OKLAHOMA...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Locally strong/gusty winds and perhaps a brief tornado or two may
   occur this afternoon/early evening across parts of southern Kansas
   into northwest Oklahoma and vicinity.

   ...Southern Kansas/Northern Oklahoma...
   Recent surface analysis shows a weak low over northwest OK/the
   northeast TX Panhandle, with a front extending northeastward from
   this low across KS. A Pacific cold front also extends southward from
   this low over the southern Plains. Cloud cover remains prevalent
   over the warm sector across the southern/central Plains late this
   morning, aided by lift associated with a mid/upper-level trough/low
   centered over the southwest KS and the OK/TX Panhandles per latest
   water vapor satellite imagery. While not a classic setup for
   non-supercell tornadoes given modest low-level lapse rates and a
   progressive cold front, there may still be a window for a brief
   tornado or two this afternoon/early evening across parts of southern
   KS into northwest OK and vicinity.

   This area should generally warm into the 70s per recent RAP/HRRR
   guidance, and even modest breaks in the cloud cover should support
   some steepening of low-level lapse rates in an otherwise
   vorticity-rich environment along/near both fronts. Current
   expectations are for cells to develop over southwest KS/northwest OK
   in the next couple of hours (by 18-20Z), with cool temperatures
   aloft (around -10 to -11 C at 500 mb) aiding updraft strength in an
   otherwise weak deep-layer shear environment. Small hail, strong to
   locally severe winds, and perhaps a brief tornado could occur with
   this activity until the southeastward-advancing cold front undercuts
   convection by late afternoon/early evening.

   ...Texas/ArkLaTex into the Mid Mississippi Valley/Midwest...
   Ongoing convection across central/north-central TX has remained
   sub-severe through the morning. A rather moist low-level airmass
   characterized by generally mid to upper 70s surface dewpoints is
   present across east/coastal TX ahead of these thunderstorms. While
   lapse rates aloft will remain poor (reference 12Z observed soundings
   from FWD/DRT), some increase in instability is anticipated
   downstream this afternoon with continued daytime heating.
   South-southwesterly low/mid-level flow will continue to gradually
   diminish through the day as the primary mid/upper-level trough
   ejects northeastward across the southern/central Plains through this
   evening. This will limit the degree of deep-layer shear available to
   support organized updrafts and overall severe potential across the
   ArkLaTex into east/south TX. That said, gusty winds may still occur
   on a localized basis as convection spreads eastward across these
   areas through the afternoon/evening.

   Modestly enhanced mid-level flow and greater deep-layer shear will
   be present this afternoon farther north into the mid MS
   Valley/Midwest, as multiple subtle mid-level vorticity maxima spread
   northeastward over these regions. However, both boundary-layer
   instability and lapse rates aloft are forecast to remain rather
   weak, which should limit updraft strength and overall severe
   potential with northward extent across these areas.

   ..Gleason/Chalmers.. 10/01/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS01 PTSDY1 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 1 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 2000Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 010548

   Day 2 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1248 AM CDT Thu Oct 01 2026

   Valid 021200Z - 031200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   No severe thunderstorms are expected across the U.S. on Friday or
   Friday night.

   ...DISCUSSION...
   West-northwesterly mid-level flow will be in place over much of the
   northern U.S. on Friday, as multiple shortwave troughs move
   east-southeastward through the flow. At the surface, a cold front
   will advance southeastward from the mid Mississippi Valley into the
   Southeast. Surface dewpoints to the south of the front over the Gulf
   Coast region will be in the 70s F. This moist airmass will become
   weakly unstable by afternoon over most areas. Isolated to scattered
   thunderstorms will be possible within zones of focused low-level
   convergence. Deep-layer shear is forecast to be relatively weak,
   which will limit any severe potential.

   ..Broyles.. 10/01/2026

SPC AC 010725

   Day 3 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0225 AM CDT Thu Oct 01 2026

   Valid 031200Z - 041200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   No severe thunderstorms are expected across the U.S. on Saturday and
   Saturday night.

   ...DISCUSSION...
   At mid-levels, zonal westerly flow will develop on Saturday from the
   northern Plains into the Northeast. In the southern U.S., mid-flow
   aloft will remain west-southwesterly. At the surface, a slow-moving
   front will remain located across the lower Mississippi and Tennessee
   Valleys. To the south of the front, weak instability is expected by
   afternoon over much of the Southeast. Isolated to scattered
   thunderstorms will be possible in areas where low-level convergence
   becomes focused. Deep-layer shear will be relatively weak across
   this moist airmass, limiting any severe potential.
